message:
The coverage holds for five functions but fails for two, Structural Dynamicist, Bridge Retrofit Engineer, Pedestrian Comfort and Safety Assessor, Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead. In plain words most functions have a choice but comfort proof has only one idea and deck look still lacks a comfort view. Capture of motion, supply of force, dissipation of energy, transfer of loads and limiting of travel each have concepts from at least two members, maintain-deck-appearance has three concepts but still owes one from Pedestrian Comfort and Safety Assessor, and verify-comfort-acceptance has only the maintenance-access assumed constraint from Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead (C25) and still owes one each from Structural Dynamicist, Bridge Retrofit Engineer and Pedestrian Comfort and Safety Assessor. The two weakest functions for cycle 2 distant-analogy mapping are verify-comfort-acceptance owned by Pedestrian Comfort and Safety Assessor with support from Structural Dynamicist, and transfer-loads-to-structure owned by Bridge Retrofit Engineer with support from Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead.

The numbers that stand still leave a buildability gap, Structural Dynamicist, Bridge Retrofit Engineer, Pedestrian Comfort and Safety Assessor, Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead. In plain words the push-back weight is tiny against crowd weight and the motion fits in a hand, the bare shake is outside everyday feel while the damped shake is inside, but nobody computed the spring sag plus impact load that sizes the under-deck space. Total Tuned Mass Damper, defined as Tuned Mass Damper (TMD), mass 800 kg from the total-mass calculation (E13) weighing 7.85 kN from the static-weight calculation (E26) against 600 kN live load from the live-load estimate (E30) sums to 1.31 percent and meets the 2 percent rule in the clamped-bracket concept (C8), peak relative travel 49.4 mm from the free-decay simulation (E17) against 80 mm stop gap in the caged-stop concept (C23) fits a hand width and girder depth, bare acceleration 8.28 m/s2 from the bare-acceleration calculation (E43) is 0.844 g almost body weight and outside footbridge feel while retrofitted 0.668 m/s2 from the retrofitted-acceleration calculation (E44) settling to 0.67 m/s2 in the crowd build-up simulation (E45) is 0.068 g inside the 0.5 to 1.0 m/s2 Medium band in the comfort-target concept (C13). I reconcile two stiffnesses by keeping modal stiffness 2.85 MN per m from the modal-stiffness calculation (E12) for 20 t and dropping 4.28 MN per m from the early modal-stiffness estimate (E9) for 30 t because all downstream tune 1.83 Hz from the optimum-frequency calculation (E14), damping 12.0 percent from the optimum-damping calculation (E15) and stroke use 20 t. The critical quantity nobody computed is static spring sag under TMD weight plus stop impact load and High-Strength Friction-Grip, defined as High-Strength Friction-Grip (HSFG), slip capacity for combined 13.1 kN static plus 5.22 kN dynamic force from the dynamic-force calculation (E29).

There are no open blocking objections, and I answer each not-ready vote as still not ready, Structural Dynamicist, Bridge Retrofit Engineer, Pedestrian Comfort and Safety Assessor, Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead. In plain words the objections about tuning, steel weight, comfort level and twin units are evidence-backed but not yet decided interfaces. Structural Dynamicist is answered by carrying tune versus stroke and effective damping about 6.20 percent from the free-decay simulation (E17) into selection, Bridge Retrofit Engineer is answered by carrying stiffening need 46.5 percent from the stiffness-increase calculation (E27) and clamp-without-weld evidence in the injection-bolt behaviour source (E24) into bracket proof, Pedestrian Comfort and Safety Assessor is answered by holding Medium comfort as working target pending my Maximum versus Medium choice with Below Bridge Access Vehicle, defined as Below Bridge Access Vehicle (BBAV), access from the inspection-access rule (E49), Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead is answered by carrying twin 400 kg units from the per-unit split (E52) weighing 3.92 kN each from the per-unit weight calculation (E53) and the under-deck layout sketch (E55) into selection.

RECORD: Decided nothing yet, numbers that stand are 40 m span with 1.9 Hz mode with TMD 800 kg total in twin 400 kg units tuned 1.83 Hz at 12.0 percent damping giving 49.4 mm stroke with 80 mm stops and 0.67 m/s2 Medium comfort versus 8.28 m/s2 bare, still open are F6 concept from Pedestrian Comfort and Safety Assessor and F7 concepts from Structural Dynamicist and Bridge Retrofit Engineer and Pedestrian Comfort and Safety Assessor plus distant analogies for F7 and F4 plus sag and impact and clamp proof from Bridge Retrofit Engineer and Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead and comfort-level choice by the Manager.
Note on Structural Dynamicist: strong tune and decay evidence with clear mass-ratio trade.
Note on Bridge Retrofit Engineer: strong stiffening-versus-damping and weight-fraction evidence, bracket proof still owed.
Note on Pedestrian Comfort and Safety Assessor: strong crowd-force and comfort-band evidence, F6 and F7 concepts still owed.
Note on Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead: strong twin-unit buildability and access evidence, impact and clearance proof still owed.
My position is not ready, because selections, comfort target and buildability proofs are still open.
